title: Research: close the mixed P112 pair-reader tariff gap
body:
Closes PR3447's mixed-list handoff. Any finite axis/nonaxis query list in one literal PR3370 indicator pair reduces to at most four directions without increasing actual reader cost. All 496 pairs retain the sharp original tariff; disjoint pair replacements cannot lower 224. No new κ.

New beyond PR3429 (at most three directions) and PR3447 (dense-only): submodular support layers plus a complete 435,456-state census for mixed lists.

Base: 6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c
Pins: PR3370 4cae85b18712b85a39905e51bde17346ccc5b805; PR3429 ffd6d6a9060e12fe7b7854f90aca7f8aa4ca211d; PR3447 924f3b50741ba2f6dc005b1dee4c9219665296f2. SOURCE hashes, proof, receipts and handoff: https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/d1703ebc3f5c0e0b47fa37066a2288367402973a/research/p112-mixed-query-reader-floor

Reproduce:
`python3 -I -Werror -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-mixed-query-reader-floor`
Expected: three scoped PASS markers and PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE.

Executed on Python 3.12.14: complete census; code-disjoint matrix/multicover replay (23,319,544 transitions); 152 exact operators; F2/F3/F5 controls; seven mathematical control groups; three optimized CLI corruptions and restored positive replay. Read-only Git-free export passes unchanged.

Scope: scalar pair-span recoding on this fixed geometry, over every field. Different rank distributions and broader recodings remain open. Native acquisition, frames, restoration, hosting, precision and full supplier/outer admission remain unproved; selected frontier and inherited assumptions unchanged. No formal or independent human review claimed.

Published d1703ebc3f5c0e0b47fa37066a2288367402973a; complete remote tree equals tested tree 0c2d9ef1d05884d0333b3619c9450d279df2a7eb. Only one isolated package changes. Claim/result recorded locally: no sprint issue or Discussion-write tool available.

Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit Tekalign/PR3370, Nick Petalas/PR3429/3447 and the predecessor lineage retained in the package. Apache-2.0.
